corrections.text: The article says "Per-token prices understate the change in cost for existing workloads" and that the tokenizer is "why Anthropic's own average-cost estimate is smaller than the per-token price cut." The roughly 30% more tokens per text mean per-token prices overstate the savings, not understate them. Anthropic's announcement (footnote 2) says the 75% average figure reflects both the price cuts (90% for requests up to 100,000 tokens, 50% above that, with about 90% of Haiku 4.5 requests in the lower bucket) and the tokenizer change, not the tokenizer alone.

The article gives OSWorld 2.1 scores without qualification. The announcement labels those figures "Offline subset", and its Sonnet 5.5 FrontierCode 1.1 (Main) figure of 52.1% is marked as Xhigh effort.
